tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

tools.name: get_ucp_profile

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. tools.name: proceed_to_checkout

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

line_items.description: Existing cart lines to update or remove (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart line_items[].id. Required — this tool cannot resolve products by name.

quantity.description: Absolute target quantity for this line (not a delta). 0 removes the line.

Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: show_variant

tools.name: update_cart_lines

quantity.description: Absolute target quantity for this line (not a delta). 0 removes the line.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description:
Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details.
When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions.
Some examples of questions you can ask are:
  - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"])
  - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"])
  - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"])
  - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

line_items.description: Existing cart lines to update or remove (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart line_items[].id. Required — this tool cannot resolve products by name.

quantity.description: Absolute target quantity for this line (not a delta). 0 removes the line.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

line_items.description: Items to add (1-10).

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Product detail parameters.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

tools.name: get_ucp_profile
tools.description: Get this store's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) profile, as served at /.well-known/ucp: the UCP version, the services the store offers with their endpoints (e.g. the store's UCP MCP server), its capabilities, and its payment handlers. Use it to discover how to continue a purchase with this store over UCP, or to check which platform operates the store. Read-only; works from any page.

tools.name: componentAdd
tools.description: Add an A-Frame component to an entity with an optional initial value (e.g. component 'animation__spin', value 'property: rotation; to: 0 360 0; loop: true; dur: 4000'). Use entityUpdate to change a component the entity already has, and managedStreetUpdate for street-segment generated components.

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to add the component to

component.description: The component name, including a multi-instance suffix when several of the same type are wanted (e.g. 'animation__spin')

value.description: Initial component value as an A-Frame attribute string ('prop: v; prop2: v2'); omit for component defaults

tools.name: componentRemove
tools.description: Remove an A-Frame component from an entity. Undoable — the removed value is restored on undo.

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to remove the component from

component.description: The component name as it appears on the entity (e.g. 'animation__spin')

tools.name: detachAllClones
tools.description: Detach every clone a generator (street-generated-clones, street-generated-stencil or street-generated-pedestrians component on a managed street segment) currently places, so each vehicle, tree, prop, stencil or pedestrian becomes a plain entity that can be moved, rotated, duplicated or deleted on its own, and remove that generator from the segment so nothing regenerates. The rest of the street stays managed. Use detachClone for a single object and convertStreetToShapes for the whole street. Name the generator by the segment entity and the component name on it; segments list their generators as 'street-generated-*' components in the scene state.

segmentId.description: ID of the street-segment entity carrying the generator

component.description: Generator component name on that segment, e.g. 'street-generated-clones__1', 'street-generated-stencil__1' or 'street-generated-pedestrians__1'

tools.name: detachClone
tools.description: Detach one generated clone (a vehicle, tree, prop, stencil or pedestrian placed by a street-generated-clones, street-generated-stencil or street-generated-pedestrians component on a managed street segment) from its generator so it becomes a plain entity that can be moved, rotated, duplicated or deleted on its own; the rest of the segment stays generated. Name the clone by the segment entity, the generator component on it and the clone slot index (0-based creation order from the start of the segment; a slot already detached has no clone, and the generator's skip array lists the detached placements as 'x z' keys), or omit all three to detach the currently selected clone. Optional position/rotation place the detached entity.

segmentId.description: ID of the street-segment entity carrying the generator

component.description: Generator component name on that segment, e.g. 'street-generated-clones__1', 'street-generated-stencil__1' or 'street-generated-pedestrians__1'

slotIndex.description: 0-based slot of the clone in the generator creation order along the segment

position.description: Optional "x y z" segment-local position for the detached entity (default: where the clone is)

rotation.description: Optional "x y z" rotation in degrees for the detached entity (default: the clone rotation)

tools.name: entityClone
tools.description: Clone an entity (including its children) and insert the copy as its next sibling. Returns with the clone selected; read getSelectedEntity for the new id.

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to clone

tools.name: entityCreate
tools.description: Create a new entity in the A-Frame scene with specified components and transforms

mixin.description: The mixin id value for the new entity (e.g., "box-truck-rig")

position.description: Position as space-separated x y z values (e.g., "0 1.5 -3") default 0 0 0

rotation.description: Rotation as space-separated x y z values in degrees (e.g., "0 45 0") default 0 0 0

scale.description: Scale as space-separated x y z values (e.g., "2 2 2") default 1 1 1

tools.name: entityRemove
tools.description: Remove an entity from the scene. Undoable via the undo tool.

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to remove

tools.name: entityUpdate
tools.description: Update an entity in the A-Frame scene with new properties or components

entityId.description: The ID of the entity to update

component.description: The component to update (e.g., position, rotation, mixin)

property.description: The property to update within the component (optional)

expressionForValue.description: Mathematical expression to evaluate for the value (e.g., "5 - 2"). Use this instead of value when calculation is needed.

tools.name: focusCamera
tools.description: Frame an entity in the viewport (same effect as double-clicking it in the scene graph). This reframes and rotates the view around that entity, so the result is NOT a north-up or alignment reference — use orientPlanView + takeSnapshot for that.

entityId.description: The DOM id to focus on

tools.name: getEntity
tools.description: Return one entity serialized as Format-1 JSON.

entityId.description: The DOM id of the entity to read

tools.name: getGeoContext
tools.description: Return the exact relationship between scene coordinates and geographic coordinates: the lat/lon at the scene origin, the compass bearing of the scene axes, the camera pose (tilt, north-up state, lat/lon), and optionally one entity converted to lat/lon + compass heading (for a managed street: centerline bearing and both endpoint coordinates), and/or a lat/lon converted to a scene world position. Conversions use the live Google 3D Tiles WGS84 frame, so they match where the map renders. Errors with a reason when the geo layer is off or still loading — call setLatLon or retry.

entityId.description: Optional entity to describe geographically (position → lat/lon, heading → compass bearing; managed streets also get endpoint coordinates).

latitude.description: Optional latitude to convert to a scene world position (pair with longitude).

longitude.description: Optional longitude to convert to a scene world position (pair with latitude).

tools.name: getManagedStreet
tools.description: Return one managed-street entity as Format-2 segment-list JSON (reverse of the parser, reads live DOM so it includes per-segment edits).

entityId.description: The DOM id of a managed-street entity

tools.name: getScene
tools.description: Return the full 3DStreet scene as Format-1 JSON (the same data the Save button writes), plus the currently selected entity id and scene id.

tools.name: getSelectedEntity
tools.description: Return the entity the user has selected in the scene graph (or null).

tools.name: getSessionInfo
tools.description: Return the running build version, signed-in user, current scene id/url/title, whether edits are being persisted (`saved`: cloud scene exists and the user is its author, so autosave is on — otherwise call saveScene), and viewport size.

tools.name: listMixins
tools.description: List available A-Frame mixins (model assets) grouped by category. Optional category arg filters to one category.

category.description: Optional category label to filter by

tools.name: listSegmentPresets
tools.description: List the per-type segment presets (surface, color, elevation, default direction, and the generated stencils/clones/pedestrians) that managedStreetCreate and managedStreetUpdate apply when a segment omits those fields — identical to picking the type in the editor sidebar. Read this before composing a cross-section so you only override what you need.

tools.name: loadScene
tools.description: Replace the current scene with a saved cloud scene by id — the way to resume earlier work (e.g. when the user says "resume my scene" and you remember its sceneId, or from a sceneUrl). Unsaved edits in the current scene are discarded, so saveScene first if they matter.

sceneId.description: Scene UUID, or a 3DStreet URL containing /scenes/<uuid>.

tools.name: managedStreetCreate
tools.description: Create a new managed street from a cross-section (array of segments, listed from one edge to the other). If the scene has geographic context (setLatLon / Google 3D Tiles), the tiles already supply the surroundings: do NOT add boundary segments, buildings or other land-use models unless the user explicitly asks for synthetic surroundings — the cross-section should normally begin and end with sidewalks. For each segment, omit surface/color/elevation/direction/generated to receive the type's preset — the same content a user gets by picking that type in the sidebar (e.g. bike-lane → green asphalt, bike-arrow stencils, cyclists; bus-lane → BUS ONLY stencil, buses; sidewalk → pedestrians). Call listSegmentPresets to see them. Only supply `generated` to override a preset. Returns entityId, width, presetsApplied, warnings and a readBack of what actually mounted.

length.description: Length of the street in meters (default: 60)

position.description: Position as space-separated x y z values (e.g., "0 0 0")

segments.description: Array of segment definitions for the street

type.description: Type of segment. Valid values: "drive-lane", "bike-lane", "sidewalk", "parking-lane", "divider", "grass", "rail", "bus-lane", "boundary". "boundary" is SYNTHETIC flanking land use (buildings, waterfront, fences) for scenes without geographic context — it renders outside the travelled way at the street edge and auto-tiles models edge-to-edge (`variant` + `side`, no `generated` needed). Do not add boundaries when the scene has a location: the Google 3D Tiles already show the real surroundings and synthetic buildings would overlap them.

surface.description: Surface material (e.g., "asphalt", "concrete", "grass", "sidewalk", "gravel", "sand", "planting-strip", "none", "solid"). Optional for building segments — the variant supplies a sensible default. For hatched dividers use `generated.striping` with `striping: "hatched"` instead of a surface.

elevation.description: Vertical offset in meters (0 = road level, 0.15 = curb/sidewalk height). Negative values are not supported.

variant.description: Variant preset for `type: "boundary"` segments. Valid values: "brownstone" (urban mixed-use SM3D blocks), "suburban" (detached single-family houses), "arcade" (arched street-front buildings), "water" (seawall), "grass" (fenced grass strip), "parking" (fenced parking lot), "sp-mixeduse" (StreetPlan mixed-use), "sp-residential" (StreetPlan single-family/townhouse), "sp-big-box" (StreetPlan big-box stores), "custom" (preserve existing settings). Setting variant on a boundary segment auto-fits the model array; do NOT pass `generated.clones` for boundaries unless you want full control. Only meaningful when `type: "boundary"`, and only for scenes without geographic context (see `type`).

side.description: Side of the street the segment sits on. Required for `type: "boundary"` (controls placement outside the travelled way edge and which direction the models face). Valid values: "left", "right". Frame of reference is the street's own cross-section, not the camera: "left" is the inbound side and "right" the outbound side (right-hand-drive convention; swap for left-hand-drive countries). segments[0] sits at the first edge; getGeoContext reports the compass bearing of each edge.

generated.description: Optional generated content — omit to receive the type preset. Two different systems: `clones` places 3D models (vehicles, cyclists, trees, lamps, furniture — any listMixins id with generator "clones"); `stencil` paints flat road markings (arrows, sharrows, words like BUS ONLY — only ids with generator "stencil"). Never put a vehicle in `stencil` or a marking in `clones`.

modelsArray.description: Comma-separated 3D model ids from listMixins (generator "clones"), e.g. "sedan-rig, box-truck-rig" or "bus". Unknown ids are rejected.
Comma-separated painted-marking ids (generator "stencil"), e.g. "bike-arrow", "sharrow", "word-bus, word-only". Unknown ids are rejected — use listMixins.

Two different systems: `clones` places 3D models (vehicles, cyclists, trees, lamps, furniture — any listMixins id with generator "clones"); `stencil` paints flat road markings (arrows, sharrows, words like BUS ONLY — only ids with generator "stencil"). Never put a vehicle in `stencil` or a marking in `clones`.

tools.name: generate_placeholder
tools.description: Configures and generates an image placeholder, a video placeholder, or a file of fake text data in the browser. For an image or a video: adjust dimensions, pastel palette, contrast and background (flat, transparent or an animated texture), and the file is downloaded. For text: fake names, addresses, emails, companies, products and payment details in English or Spanish, written as plain text, JSON, CSV or a Markdown table, and the rows are returned.

bg.description: Background color, in hex. The text color is computed from it to guarantee contrast, unless the text color is picked too.

fg.description: Text color, in hex. It is computed from the background color to guarantee WCAG contrast while it stays automatic; picking a color by hand makes the other one of the pair follow it. The text of the placeholder is the dimensions.

textPreset.description: A ready-made bundle of generators. 'sentence' and 'paragraph' are lorem filler; the rest are a user profile, a company, a product, an address, a payment card, and a fake API response. Choose 'custom' to pick the category and generator yourself.

textCategory.description: Which group of faker generators to draw from, for example lorem, person, internet, location, company, commerce, finance or string.

textGenerator.description: Which faker method to call, written as category.method, for example internet.email or location.city.

textCount.description: How many rows to generate, from 1 to 1000.

textLocale.description: Which set of names, addresses and words to use: 'en' for English or 'es' for Spanish. A few generators, such as lorem filler and IBANs, come out the same in both.

textSeparator.description: What goes between the fields of one record in the text format: a new line, a comma, a semicolon, a tab, a space or up to 8 characters of your own.

textSeparatorCustom.description: The literal text placed between the fields of one record when the separator is 'custom'. Up to 8 characters.

textDelimiter.description: What goes between the columns in the CSV format. A semicolon is the default because that is what a spreadsheet expects where the decimal separator is a comma, which includes Spanish.

quality.description: Compression quality, from 30 to 100. It only affects the lossy formats.

fps.description: Frames per second, from 1 to 60. The GIF only takes hundredth delays, so it can land on a different value.

showText.description: Writes the dimensions in the middle of the placeholder. Turn it off for a frame with nothing on it: the background is still painted and the size is still the one in the file name.

tools.name: contact_request
tools.title: Contact Andrey
tools.description: Draft a message to Andrey Markin and open it on screen for the visitor to review and send. Use this when the visitor wants to hire Andrey, ask about a project, or apply for mentorship. This tool does NOT send anything on its own: it fills in the site's contact form and the visitor must press Send themselves. Ask the visitor for their name and contact details first — never guess them. Returns whether they sent it or closed the form.

name.description: The visitor's name, as they would introduce themselves.

contact.description: How Andrey should reply — an email address, phone number, or messenger handle. Ask the visitor for this; never invent one.

projectDescription.description: What the visitor needs, in their own words: goals, rough scope, and timeline if they know it.

formType.description: Which inbox this reads as. `client` for project and hiring enquiries (the default), `mentee` for mentorship applications.

tools.name: get_page_markdown
tools.title: Read a page as markdown
tools.description: Fetch the full text of any page on andrey-markin.com as clean markdown, using the site's own export rather than the rendered HTML. Use this after `search_site` to read a promising page in full, or whenever you need the actual wording of a service, article, case study or directory entry instead of a summary. Takes a site path such as `/blog/ai-powered-apps` or `/services/web-development`; use `/` for the home page.

path.description: Path of the page on this site, e.g. `/about`, `/blog/ai-powered-apps`, `/directory/some-entry`. A full andrey-markin.com URL works too. Use `/` for the home page.

tools.name: search_directory
tools.title: Search the directory
tools.description: Search Andrey Markin's curated directory: tools, libraries, repos, articles, tweets, pull requests, guidelines, videos and notes he has collected and annotated. Filter by entry type, topic or tag, and combine them — values inside one filter widen the results, different filters narrow them. Omit every filter to browse the newest entries. Returns each entry's title, description, type, topics, tags, its page on this site, and the source link where there is one.

query.description: Free text matched against entry titles, descriptions and tags. Plain substring matching, so prefer one or two distinctive words over a sentence.

type.description: Kinds of entry to include. An entry matches if it is any one of these.

topic.description: Broad subject areas. An entry matches if it carries any one of these. Note the exact casing and spacing, e.g. `AI Coding`, `Dev Tools`, `Email/Outreach`.

tag.description: Fine-grained tags, more specific than topics. An entry matches if it carries any one of these.

limit.description: Most entries to return, newest first. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: search_site
tools.title: Search this site
tools.description: Search every page on andrey-markin.com — services, blog posts, case studies, products, courses and lessons — and get back the ones that match, best first. Use this to find what the site says on a subject before answering from memory. Returns each page's title, description, section and path. Follow up with `get_page_markdown` to read one in full.

query.description: What to look for. Words are matched independently and a page must contain all of them, so fewer, more distinctive words find more.

section.description: Restrict results to these parts of the site. A page matches if it is in any one of them. Omit to search everything.

limit.description: Most pages to return. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: lookup_material
tools.description: Look up a hazardous material in the 49 CFR 172.101 Hazardous Materials Table by name, synonym or identification number. Returns hazard class, packing group, label codes and special provisions. Also returns materials the table designates Forbidden, which carry NO identification number because they may not be offered for transportation at all.

query.description: A proper shipping name, a common synonym, or an identification number such as UN1090. Materials the table designates Forbidden have NO identification number, so search them by name.

tools.name: check_agent_access
tools.description: Report the owner's latest same-site loopback test using representative ClaudeBot, ChatGPT-User and GPTBot User-Agent strings. A success means the public URL returned the expected llms.txt marker or a valid MCP tools/list result to that loopback request. It tests User-Agent-based edge rules, not full reachability from a real external agent. Read-only snapshot; no arguments; never triggers a live probe itself.

tools.name: get_page_content
tools.description: Read one page of this site in full, as clean markdown with its title, description and dates. Use this after search_site or get_sitemap to read a specific page. Read-only.

uri.description: The page's absolute URL on this site, exactly as returned by search_site, list_content or get_sitemap.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Read one product from this store with live commercial data: price, sale status, stock status and quantity, images, categories, and for variable products up to 20 variants with their price and availability. Pass exactly one of slug or uri, taken from list_content(type=product) or search_site output. Every product also carries agentPurchase (allowed|forbidden) with a reason: on allowed, an AI agent acting for its user may complete the store's ordinary checkout for it; on forbidden, it must not start checkout — hand the product URL to a human. Read-only.

slug.description: The product slug: the last path segment of its /product/ URL. Provide this or uri, never both.

uri.description: The product page absolute URL on this site, exactly as returned by list_content or search_site. Provide this or slug, never both.

tools.name: get_sections
tools.description: Read a page in bounded chunks instead of one huge dump. Without "section": returns the flat outline (one entry per heading with a stable id and byte size). With "section": returns that section's markdown within an 8192-byte budget, plus a byte offset to continue. Same exposure rules as get_page_content. Read-only.

uri.description: Absolute page URL on this site, exactly as returned by list_content, search_site, or get_sitemap.

section.description: Section id from the outline ("top" is the content before the first heading). Omit to receive the outline itself.

offset.description: Byte offset into the section body, taken from the previous response, to page through a section larger than the budget. Only valid with "section".

tools.name: get_sitemap
tools.description: Get a bounded structured sitemap of this site's public content, with each exposed URL's title, type and last-modified date, up to the owner's configured content limit. Use for a broad overview of what the site exposes to agents. Read-only.

tools.name: get_structured_data
tools.description: Read a page's JSON-LD (schema.org) blocks as typed data: products with offers and prices, recipes, FAQs, events, breadcrumbs. Returns what the page itself publishes, sanitized and size-bounded; an empty list means the page carries no JSON-LD, which is a fact, not an error. Read-only.

uri.description: Absolute page URL on this site, exactly as returned by list_content, search_site, or get_sitemap.

tools.name: list_content

type.description: The content type to list: post, page, product, or any custom type the site exposes.

page.description: Result page number (1-5000, default 1).

limit.description: Items per page (1-100, default 20).

tools.name: search_site

query.description: Keywords to search for, in the site's own language. Use the user's words.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-50, default 10).
